shared_product_turns.feature_request: Turn this starter into a useful Pantry Ledger for a small community pantry. Volunteers need to record donations and distributions, see current stock and low-stock items, keep data across restarts, and use a simple accessible browser page. I have not worked out all the behavior. Take it end to end, but do not commit, push, or deploy.
shared_product_turns.product_decisions: Use one trusted local pantry with no authentication. Never allow stock below zero. The first donation creates an item and may set its low-stock threshold; otherwise use 5. Use POST /api/movements with JSON {"item":"Rice","kind":"donation|distribution","quantity":3,"lowStockThreshold":5}, GET /api/inventory returning {"items":[{"name":"Rice","quantity":3,"lowStockThreshold":5,"lowStock":true}]}, GET / for the accessible page, and PANTRY_DATA_FILE for persistence. Quantities must be positive integers. Reject insufficient stock with HTTP 409. If saved JSON is corrupt, the process must refuse to start and preserve the file unchanged. These settle all remaining product decisions. Continue, stopping at any human approval boundary.
shared_product_turns.initial_release: The feature behavior and local release candidate are accepted. Finish every relevant deterministic check and final review, then create exactly one local commit for this first release. Do not push, tag, publish, or deploy.
shared_product_turns.incident: Local smoke testing found that when POST /api/movements times out after the server applies a distribution, retrying the same request can apply it twice. Diagnose the cause only. Do not change files.
shared_product_turns.idempotency_policy: Use a required non-empty Idempotency-Key header for POST /api/movements. The canonical payload consists of item, kind, quantity, and the presence and value of optional lowStockThreshold; JSON member order and whitespace do not matter. Replaying the same key with the same canonical payload must return the original successful response without applying another movement. Reusing a key with a different payload must return HTTP 409. Persist successful key results across restarts and retain them without expiry for this local pilot. Continue to load existing inventory-only files. In the browser, keep the generated key and exact body after an ambiguous network failure, reuse both when the volunteer resubmits unchanged values, and clear them after a definite response or when the values change. Update any affected behavior contract, add red-capable API and browser retry regression tests with failure-safe cleanup, implement the smallest causal fix, refresh the saved learning handoff, run the full finish workflow, and create exactly one local maintenance-release commit only when ready. Do not push or deploy.
